intended_object: For an `R`-linear isomorphism e : M ≅ N, the induced isomorphism of schemes Proj(Sym_R N) ≅ Proj(Sym_R M), i.e. the isomorphism of projective spaces P(N) ≅ P(M) that comes from functoriality of Proj applied to the graded isomorphism Sym(e). I took this from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body takes the graded ring maps Sym(e) and Sym(e⁻¹). The two lemmas just above the definition (`symmetricAlgebraGradedMap_comp_symm` and `symmetricAlgebraGradedMap_symm_comp`) prove that these maps are inverse to each other. The library's `projIsoOfInverseGradedRingHom` then turns this pair into an isomorphism of `Proj` schemes, which is the standard construction. The isomorphism goes in the contravariant direction, Proj(Sym N) ≅ Proj(Sym M), as it should, because Proj is contravariant.

The only restriction is that M and N must live in the same universe. This is not a real loss of generality. An isomorphism `≅` in `Scheme` needs both schemes in the same category `Scheme.{max u v}`. `Proj` of Sym(M) and of Sym(N) live in the same category only when the carrier universes agree, and `Proj.map` needs this too. For other universe choices, the related definitions in the same file that build bijections on points and on closed points already allow independent universes.

The coefficient ring is an arbitrary commutative ring and the modules are arbitrary, which is the natural generality. I found no Mathlib declaration that gives this isomorphism directly.
